key_insight: MM-CondChain introduces a programmatically verified benchmark that tests MLLMs on deeply chained, visually grounded conditional workflows — including branching and early termination — revealing gaps not captured by prior shallow-composition benchmarks.
problem_solved: Existing multimodal benchmarks focus on shallow compositions or independent constraints and fail to evaluate the ability of models to verify and follow long, conditional visual workflows (e.g., GUI tasks) where decisions depend on chained visual conditions and execution may branch or stop early.
method: Design a dataset of procedurally generated multimodal scenarios that require chained, compositional visual conditions and action decisions (branching and termination).
Employ a programmatic verifier / execution engine to simulate ground-truth workflow execution and automatically validate model outputs against expected conditional branches and end states.
Benchmark multiple MLLMs with metrics that measure correctness across chain depth, branching complexity, and termination accuracy to surface failure modes.
impact: Provides a reliable, reproducible way to measure and improve MLLMs' ability to perform real-world visual workflows that require precise conditional reasoning, aiding safer and more robust deployment in GUI automation and other multimodal decision-making systems.

paper_title: MM-CondChain: A Programmatically Verified Benchmark for Visually Grounded Deep Compositional Reasoning
paper_authors: Haozhan Shen, Shilin Yan, Hongwei Xue, Shuaiqi Lu, Xiaojun Tang
